title: Aubergine Lasagne
subtitle: Layered baked pasta with fried aubergine and tomato
excerpt: Lasagne layers with fried aubergine in place of meat, in a rich tomato sauce with mozzarella and parmesan. Substantial, deeply flavoured, and good the next day.

recipe.sourceNotes: Aubergine lasagne is a southern Italian and Italian-American adaptation that replaces meat ragù with fried aubergine, drawing on the flavours of melanzane alla parmigiana. It became widely popular across Italy and internationally as vegetarian eating grew during the late twentieth century.

content.text: Aubergine lasagne works when the aubergine is fried properly rather than roasted or baked into mush. Salt the slices, let them drain for 30 minutes, then fry in hot olive oil in batches until they are deep golden on both sides. They go into the layers soft but with some structure. The tomato sauce should be thick enough not to make the pasta soggy.

Salt the aubergine slices and leave in a colander for 30 minutes. Pat dry with kitchen paper. Fry in batches in hot olive oil over medium-high heat until golden brown on both sides, 3 to 4 minutes per side. Drain on kitchen paper.

Make the tomato sauce: fry the garlic in 2 tablespoons of olive oil for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes, season with salt and pepper, and simmer for 20 minutes until thick. Stir in the basil leaves.
Heat the oven to 190 C / fan 170 C / gas 5. If using dried lasagne sheets, par-cook in salted boiling water for 4 minutes and lay on clean tea towels.

Assemble: spread a layer of tomato sauce in the dish. Add a layer of pasta, then aubergine slices, torn mozzarella, a scatter of parmesan, and more tomato sauce. Repeat until the ingredients are used up, finishing with tomato sauce and a generous layer of parmesan.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the top is deep golden and the edges are bubbling. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.
